metrics.name: defender.mdo.rules
metrics.description: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 / EOP protection rules, by rule family and state. Every (rule_family, state) pair is seeded to 0 for a family that was successfully read, so a rule appearing where none existed is a change from 0 rather than a series materializing from nothing. A family whose fetch FAILED this cycle emits no point at all — a failed fetch is a gap, not a measured zero.

metrics.name: defender.mdo.rules.conditions
metrics.description: MDO/EOP rules by rule family and which recipient condition they carry (sent_to, sent_to_member_of, recipient_domain_is, except_sent_to, except_sent_to_member_of, except_recipient_domain_is). The recipient VALUES are twin-only (#112); this counts only which condition KIND is present.

metrics.name: defender.mdo.rules.unscoped
metrics.description: ENABLED MDO/EOP rules per rule family with no recipient condition on any include axis (SentTo, SentToMemberOf, RecipientDomainIs) — rules that apply org-wide. Every successfully-read rule_family is seeded to 0; a family whose fetch failed this cycle emits no point.

metrics.name: defender.mdo.unreferenced_policies
metrics.description: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 / EOP policies not referenced by any ENABLED rule, by policy type — a configured control nothing currently applies. Suppressed entirely (no points emitted) for a cycle where any of the seven policy fetches failed, rather than reporting a false zero.

metrics.name: intune.cloud_pki.authorities
metrics.description: Intune Cloud PKI certification authorities by type (root/issuing) and status. Per-CA detail — decoded subject and issuer, key platform, CRL and SCEP endpoints — on the intune.cloud_pki_authority log twin.

metrics.name: intune.cloud_pki.days_until_expiry

metrics.name: intune.cloud_pki.leaf_certificates
metrics.description: Leaf certificates issued by each Intune Cloud PKI certification authority, by status (active/expired/revoked). Which device and user each certificate belongs to is on the intune.cloud_pki_leaf_certificate log twin.

metrics.name: intune.defender.protection_state

metrics.name: intune.defender_agents.product_status
metrics.description: Intune managed devices by Windows Defender ProductStatus flag, from the DefenderAgents export report. ProductStatus is a bitmask: a device setting several flags is counted under each, so these points are independent counts and can sum to more than the fleet size.

metrics.name: intune.detected_apps.catalog_size
metrics.description: Total distinct app/version/platform rows in the Intune detectedApps catalog.

metrics.name: intune.detected_apps.device_count
metrics.description: Devices reporting a detected app installed, by app name and platform, summed across versions. Bounded by the central cardinality limiter: past cardinality.per_metric_limit the top apps by device count are kept and the tail folds into app_name="other".

metrics.name: intune.device_attestation.devices

metrics.name: intune.device_boot_security.devices

metrics.name: intune.device_encryption.devices

metrics.name: intune.device_encryption.policy_state

metrics.name: intune.devices.count
metrics.description: Intune managed device fleet count, by compliance state and operating system.

metrics.name: intune.devices.encrypted.count

metrics.name: intune.devices_without_compliance_policy.devices

metrics.name: intune.remediation.overview.remediated_device_count

metrics.description: Intune proactive-remediation device run states, counted by remediation, detection state and remediation state; per-device detail (device, OS, the detection script's output) on the intune.remediation_run_states log twin.

metrics.description: Windows PowerShell / macOS shell script run outcomes, by script, OS, target (device or user context) and run state.

metrics.description: Per-security-baseline device state from deviceStateSummary, by baseline and state.

metrics.description: Intune Settings Catalog configuration policy count, by platform, technology, and template family.

metrics.description: Seconds until a paused Windows Update ring's pause expires, by ring and update type.

metrics.description: Windows Update ring rollback-active state (1=active, 0=inactive), by ring and update type.

metrics.name: intune.update_ring.status
metrics.description: Windows Update ring device rollout status rollup, by ring and state.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.anomaly_count
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics anomaly count by severity.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.app_crash_count
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics app crash count by client executable. Bounded by the central cardinality limiter: past cardinality.per_metric_limit the top executables by crash count are kept and the tail folds into app_name="other".

metrics.name: intune.uxa.app_health.active_device_count
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics count of devices actively reporting application health, by OS version.

metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics device count, by application health state.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.baseline_score
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics baseline overall score, by baseline.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.battery_health.device_count
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics device count, by battery health state.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.battery_health_score
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics device battery health score (0-100), by health state; the -1 'not enough data' sentinel is excluded.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.boot_time_ms
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics device boot time, by restart category; the -1 'not enough data' sentinel is excluded.

metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics device count, by overall Endpoint Analytics health state.

metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics per-device score distribution (0-100), by score category.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.login_time_ms
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics device login time, by restart category; the -1 'not enough data' sentinel is excluded.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.model_device_count
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics scored-device count per device model. Microsoft publishes buckets as small as one device, so this is the real bucket size, not a floor.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.model_score
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics score (0-100) per device model, by score category. Bounded by the number of distinct (model, manufacturer) pairs in the fleet; the -1 'not enough data' sentinel is excluded rather than emitted as a negative score.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.resource_performance.device_count
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics device count, by resource performance health state.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.resource_performance_score
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics device resource performance score (0-100), by health state; the -1 'not enough data' sentinel is excluded.

metrics.name: intune.uxa.work_from_anywhere.device_count
metrics.description: Intune Endpoint Analytics device count by Windows 11 upgrade eligibility and health state; per-device readiness detail on the intune.device_work_from_anywhere log twin.

metrics.description: Windows Update for Business deployments by EFFECTIVE state, REQUESTED state and the kind of catalog entry being deployed. The two states are separate dimensions because they disagree in the interesting case — a series where they differ is a deployment not doing what was asked; per-deployment detail, including the reasons the effective state differs, on the intune.windows_update_deployment log twin.

metrics.name: intune.windows_updates.update_policies
metrics.description: Windows Update for Business deployment-service update policies by auto-enrollment update category (quality/driver/feature; `none` for a policy enrolled in none). A policy enrolled in SEVERAL categories counts once in each, so a sum over this metric is not the policy count; per-policy detail — approval rules, content filters, user experience and audience — on the intune.windows_update_policy log twin.

metrics.name: intune.wip.policy.count
metrics.description: Legacy Windows Information Protection (WIP) policy count (windowsInformationProtectionPolicies + mdmWindowsInformationProtectionPolicies), by assignment state.

metrics.name: m365.collaboration_activity.actions
metrics.description: Sum, across all users, of each workload's collaboration action counts for the report period.

metrics.name: m365.collaboration_activity.shared_externally
metrics.description: Sum, across all users, of files shared externally — the alertable external-sharing signal, as its own series so it needs no aggregation over the actions gauge.

metrics.name: m365.collaboration_activity.users
metrics.description: Count of licensed users per (workload, derived activity_state) bucket: active (activity within the report window), inactive (activity outside it), never_active (no Last Activity Date on record).

metrics.name: m365.collaboration_activity.users.deleted
metrics.description: Count of users marked deleted in the workload's usage report.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.accepted_domains
metrics.description: Exchange Online accepted domains by domain type and whether each is the tenant's default domain. domain_type and is_default_domain are both bounded by the API (a small enum and a strict boolean); the domain NAME itself lives on the m365.exchange_accepted_domain log twin only, never here (#112).

metrics.name: m365.exchange.audit_bypass.enabled_count
metrics.description: Exchange Online mailbox audit-bypass associations with AuditBypassEnabled=true — mailboxes producing NO mailbox audit records. The healthy steady state is zero. Per-mailbox identity is never a label here (#112); see the m365.exchange_audit_bypass log twin, emitted only for associations counted in this gauge.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.audit_bypass.examined
metrics.description: Exchange Online mailbox audit-bypass associations this poll classified true/false. Excludes rows where AuditBypassEnabled was absent from the wire (indeterminate, counted in neither gauge). Compare against m365.exchange.audit_bypass.enabled_count: a healthy tenant reads examined>0, enabled_count=0 — examined=0 means the source call returned nothing, not that the tenant is clean.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.audit_config.enabled
metrics.description: Exchange Online audit posture as a 0/1 flag per setting: unified_audit_log_ingestion (when off, m365.activity and m365.unified_audit silently return nothing) and admin_audit_log.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.connection_filter.ip_allow_list_length
metrics.description: The tenant's DEFAULT connection filter policy's IPAllowList entry count. Emitted as a measured 0 when empty (this project's healthy default), never omitted — a vanished series and a measured zero are different facts. Individual IPs are per-entity data and are never a label here (#112); see the m365.exchange_connection_filter_policy log twin.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.connection_filter.ip_block_list_length
metrics.description: The tenant's DEFAULT connection filter policy's IPBlockList entry count. Emitted as a measured 0 when empty, never omitted. Individual IPs are per-entity data and are never a label here (#112); see the m365.exchange_connection_filter_policy log twin.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.connection_filter.policies
metrics.description: Exchange Online connection filter policies by whether each is the tenant's default policy and whether Microsoft's dynamic safe list is enabled. Both dimensions are strict booleans; the policy NAME/identity and its IP lists live on the m365.exchange_connection_filter_policy log twin only, never here (#112).

metrics.name: m365.exchange.connectors
metrics.description: Exchange Online mail-flow connectors by direction and enabled state. All four series are seeded, so a connector appearing on a tenant that had none is a change from 0 rather than a new series. A connector is mail ROUTING — an outbound one can send the tenant's mail through infrastructure Microsoft does not own, and an inbound one can let mail arrive pre-trusted. Which connector, where it points and whether it demands TLS live on the m365.exchange_connector log twin.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.connectors.without_tls
metrics.description: Exchange Online connectors that do not require TLS, by direction. Mail crossing such a connector is neither encrypted nor authenticated in transit, so an inbound one is a channel for mail to arrive pre-trusted over cleartext.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.dkim.signing
metrics.description: Accepted domains counted by outbound DKIM signing enablement and configuration status.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.mailboxes
metrics.description: Exchange Online mailboxes by recipient type, whether forwarding is configured and whether auditing is on. Keyed by mailbox TYPE, never by mailbox — which mailbox forwards where is on the m365.exchange_mailbox log twin.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.mailboxes.setting_enabled
metrics.description: Mailboxes with each named boolean setting ON. Every setting is seeded, so "how many mailboxes have single-item recovery OFF" is the mailbox total minus this series rather than a missing one.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.org_config.setting_enabled
metrics.description: Exchange Online organization settings as a 0/1 flag per setting, named from the wire field so the polarity reads off the name (audit_disabled=1 means org-wide mailbox auditing is OFF). A setting the tenant has not configured arrives null and is OMITTED rather than reported as 0.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.outbound_spam.policies
metrics.description: Exchange Online outbound spam filter policies by whether each is the tenant's default policy and whether it is enabled. Both dimensions are strict booleans; the policy NAME/identity lives on the m365.exchange_outbound_spam_policy log twin only, never here (#112).

metrics.name: m365.exchange.outbound_spam.recipient_limit
metrics.description: The tenant's DEFAULT outbound spam policy's three recipient-limit thresholds, keyed by limit (external_per_hour/internal_per_hour/per_day). Sourced from the default policy only, even when custom policies exist — see the package doc. Absent entirely when this poll returned no policy with is_default=true.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.remote_domains
metrics.description: Exchange Online remote domains by whether they permit automatic external forwarding. The entry whose domain is "*" covers EVERY remote domain, so a non-zero true bucket may be one tenant-wide hole rather than a narrow exception — which domain it is lives on the m365.exchange_remote_domain log twin.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.transport_rules
metrics.description: Exchange Online transport rules by state and rule mode. Disabled rules are counted too: a staged rule is one toggle from live. Which rule, and what it does, is on the m365.exchange_transport_rule log twin.

metrics.name: m365.exchange.transport_rules.redirecting
metrics.description: Transport rules that blind-copy, copy, redirect or add a recipient — a message reaching someone the sender did not address. An ENABLED one is the textbook business-email-compromise persistence shape and also emits an Error-severity log record naming the target.

metrics.name: m365.inbox_rules.mailboxes_covered
metrics.description: Mailboxes this cycle actually polled for inbox rules. Compare against m365.inbox_rules.mailboxes_total: covered < total means the exo_per_mailbox cap left part of the tenant unpolled this cycle, not that the tenant is small.

metrics.name: m365.inbox_rules.mailboxes_total
metrics.description: Total mailboxes this tenant has, per Get-Mailbox. Always emitted alongside mailboxes_covered so partial coverage is never indistinguishable from a genuinely small tenant.

metrics.name: m365.inbox_rules.rules
metrics.description: Inbox rules across every polled mailbox (Get-InboxRule -IncludeHidden), counted by enabled, has_forwarding (any of ForwardTo/ForwardAsAttachmentTo/RedirectTo non-empty) and deletes (DeleteMessage=true). Never labeled by mailbox or rule identity (#112) — see the m365.inbox_rule log twin for per-rule detail.

metrics.name: m365.mailbox.delegation.assignments
metrics.description: Standing FullAccess/SendAs mailbox delegation assignments this poll examined, bucketed by kind (full_access|send_as), trustee_kind (self|delegated) and is_inherited (true|false|unknown). trustee_kind=self is the implicit NT AUTHORITY\SELF permission present on every mailbox, counted here but never given a log twin — see the package doc. Mailbox and trustee identity are never labels (#112); see the m365.mailbox_delegation log twin for those.

metrics.name: m365.mailbox.delegation.mailboxes_covered
metrics.description: Mailboxes this cycle actually polled for delegation, bounded by exo_per_mailbox's cap. See m365.mailbox.delegation.mailboxes_total.

metrics.name: m365.mailbox.delegation.mailboxes_total
metrics.description: Mailboxes the tenant actually has, per Get-Mailbox. Compare against m365.mailbox.delegation.mailboxes_covered: covered < total means this cycle's assignment gauge and twins are a PARTIAL view, not a complete one.

metrics.name: m365.mailbox_usage.quota_status.mailboxes
metrics.description: Count of mailboxes per Exchange quota-status bucket (Microsoft's own under_limit/warning_issued/send_prohibited/send_receive_prohibited/indeterminate vocabulary).

metrics.name: m365.mailbox_usage.storage_used_bytes
metrics.description: Tenant-wide Exchange mailbox storage used, in bytes.

metrics.name: m365.message_trace.bytes
metrics.description: Total size of the messages ingested from the Exchange Online message trace, by delivery status.

metrics.name: m365.message_trace.messages
metrics.description: Messages ingested from the Exchange Online message trace, by delivery status. Per-message detail (sender, recipient, subject, message id) is on the m365.message_trace log twin, never here.

metrics.name: m365.service_health.issues.total
metrics.description: Count of M365 service-health issues by classification and status.

metrics.name: m365.service_health.services.total
metrics.description: Count of M365 services in each health status.

metrics.name: m365.service_health.status
metrics.description: Numeric health-status enum per M365 service (0 = operational, higher = worse, -1 = unmapped). See docs/signals.md.

metrics.name: m365.service_messages.total
metrics.description: Count of active M365 message-center posts by category and severity.

metrics.name: m365.sharepoint.deleted_user_retention_days
metrics.description: Retention period for a deleted user's personal site, in days.

metrics.name: m365.sharepoint.external_resharing_enabled
metrics.description: 1 if external users may re-share content that was shared with them, else 0.

metrics.name: m365.sharepoint.idle_session_signout_enabled
metrics.description: 1 if idle-session sign-out is enabled for SharePoint/OneDrive, else 0.

metrics.name: m365.sharepoint.legacy_auth_enabled
metrics.description: 1 if legacy authentication protocols are enabled tenant-wide (a security risk), else 0.

metrics.name: m365.sharepoint.personal_site_storage_limit_mb
metrics.description: Default per-user OneDrive storage limit, in MB.

metrics.name: m365.sharepoint.sharing
metrics.description: Constant 1 carrying the tenant's external-sharing posture as bounded attributes.

metrics.name: m365.sharepoint.sharing_allowed_domains
metrics.description: Count of domains on the external-sharing allow list.

metrics.name: m365.sharepoint.sharing_blocked_domains
metrics.description: Count of domains on the external-sharing block list.

metrics.name: m365.sharepoint.site_storage_limit_mb
metrics.description: Default per-site SharePoint storage limit, in MB.

metrics.name: m365.sharepoint.unmanaged_sync_restricted
metrics.description: 1 if the OneDrive sync app is restricted to managed/domain-joined devices, else 0.

metrics.name: m365.storage.drives.total
metrics.description: Count of drives per derived quota state (normal <75% used, nearing >=75%, critical >=90%, exceeded >=100%).

metrics.name: m365.storage.total_bytes
metrics.description: Tenant SharePoint storage quota (pooled ceiling), in bytes.

metrics.name: m365.storage.used_bytes
metrics.description: Tenant SharePoint storage used, in bytes.

metrics.name: m365.teams.channels.total
metrics.description: Teams channels by membership type and archived state.

metrics.name: m365.teams.installed_apps.total
metrics.description: Teams installed apps by distribution method and whether they hold RSC grants.

metrics.name: m365.teams.membership.total
metrics.description: Tenant-wide Teams membership count by role.

metrics.name: m365.teams.ownerless.total
metrics.description: Teams with zero owners (excluding archived) — unmanageable orphans.

metrics.name: m365.teams.total
metrics.description: Total Teams by visibility.

metrics.name: m365.teams.with_guests.total
metrics.description: Teams with at least one external guest — a data-egress exposure surface.

metrics.name: mdca.cloud_discovery.apps
metrics.description: Cloud Discovery apps discovered from uploaded traffic logs in the trailing 30 days, by category.

metrics.name: mdca.cloud_discovery.apps.by_risk
metrics.description: Cloud Discovery apps discovered in the trailing 30 days, by risk band (this collector's own low/medium/high/critical banding of riskScore).

metrics.name: mdca.cloud_discovery.apps_truncated
metrics.description: Count of Cloud Discovery upload streams whose discovered-app list hit the per-poll cap. Non-zero means some discovered apps for that stream were not processed this cycle.

metrics.name: mdca.cloud_discovery.log_files.total
metrics.description: Sum of logFileCount across every Cloud Discovery upload stream. Unlabeled: a per-stream figure would key a series by stream identity, which grows with tenant configuration.

metrics.name: mdca.cloud_discovery.streams
metrics.description: Cloud Discovery upload streams configured for the tenant, by whether the stream is a one-off snapshot report.

metrics.name: mdca.discovery.parse.cloud_services
metrics.description: Distinct cloud apps discovered in a Cloud Discovery input stream's last successful parse.

metrics.name: mdca.discovery.parse.last_success.age
metrics.description: Seconds since a Cloud Discovery input stream last parsed successfully (alert-on-silence).

metrics.name: mdca.discovery.parse.tasks
metrics.description: Count of terminal MDCA Cloud Discovery parse tasks, by stream, template and outcome.

metrics.name: mdca.discovery.parse.transactions
metrics.description: Transactions discovered in a Cloud Discovery input stream's last successful parse.

metrics.name: purview.dlp.policies
metrics.description: DLP policies, by enforcement mode (Enforce vs audit/test/disabled).

metrics.name: purview.dlp.policy.last_changed_age
metrics.description: Seconds since the most recently changed DLP policy (max over whenChangedUtc).

metrics.name: purview.dlp.policy_bindings
metrics.description: DLP policy bindings, by workload and binding type.

metrics.name: purview.dlp.rules
metrics.description: DLP rules, by target workload and action.

metrics.name: purview.ediscovery.case_health.cases_covered
metrics.description: eDiscovery cases actually polled for case-health detail this cycle. Compare against purview.ediscovery.case_health.cases_total: covered < total means DefaultMaxCases left part of the tenant's case inventory unpolled this cycle, not that the tenant has few cases.

metrics.name: purview.ediscovery.case_health.cases_total
metrics.description: Total eDiscovery cases this tenant has, per the case list. Always emitted alongside cases_covered so partial coverage is never indistinguishable from a genuinely small tenant.

metrics.name: purview.ediscovery.case_operations
metrics.description: eDiscovery case operations across every covered case, counted by action and status. Never labeled by case or operation identity (#112).

metrics.name: purview.ediscovery.cases
metrics.description: Purview eDiscovery cases, counted per case status.

metrics.name: purview.ediscovery.custodians
metrics.description: eDiscovery custodians across every covered case — a plain count, no field mapper. Every case observed live returns zero rows; see the package doc for why no ediscoveryCustodian shape is mapped. Absent entirely when no case's fetch succeeded, so a total read failure never reads as a measured zero (#240).

metrics.name: purview.ediscovery.hold_sources
metrics.description: eDiscovery legal-hold data sources (userSources + siteSources) across every covered case, counted by which collection the row came from and its dataSourceHoldStatus. Never labeled by case, hold or source identity (#112).

metrics.name: purview.ediscovery.legal_holds
metrics.description: eDiscovery legal holds across every covered case, counted by isEnabled and whether the hold's errors array is non-empty. legalHold.status is null on every hold observed live, so it does not bucket this gauge — see AttrHoldState on the log twin. Never labeled by case or hold identity (#112).

metrics.name: purview.ediscovery.noncustodial_data_sources
metrics.description: eDiscovery non-custodial data sources across every covered case — a plain count, no field mapper. Absent entirely when no case's fetch succeeded (#240).

metrics.name: purview.labels.count
metrics.description: Purview sensitivity labels, counted per applicability target (a multi-target label counts in each).

metrics.name: purview.retention.event_types.count
metrics.description: Purview retention event types configured for the tenant.

metrics.name: purview.retention.labels.count
metrics.description: Purview retention labels, by retention behavior, post-retention action, and trigger.
